newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares hit two-year high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares hit two-year high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit a two-year high on Tuesday with increases across the board.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index added 1.5 points to 244.48, its highest level since mid-November 1994. Turnover was an average 20.56 million pounds ($6.05 million).

Broker Sherif Cararah of EFG Hermes said one feature of the day was a 1.00 rise in Suez Cement to 51.00, apparently in anticipation of the global depositary receipt (GDR) offering which Salomon Brothers is arranging.

National Bank of Egypt (NBE) chairman Mahmoud Abdelaziz told Reuters last week all the details of the GDR should be announced by the end of this month. NBE is one of the public-sector banks selling some of its Suez Cement shares.
Commercial International Bank jumped 20.00 pounds to 466.00 pounds in active trade dominated by one deal worth 675,000 pounds ($200,000).
Most shares slipped back in the milling sector, the dominant sector for some months, but Cararah said this against the overall trend, which remained strongly upwards.
"The clearing and settlement system is starting to perform better and this brings liquidity and is helping prices up. We haven't seen such activity for a while," he said.
The biggest rise was in al-Ahram Beverages, also known as Pyramids Breweries, which has been bought by a consortium including foreign funds. The shares closed almost six percent up, at 71.01 pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose just over one percent, to 365.51 from 361.69 points on Monday, andd the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 172.53 from 171.89.
